title: Role based authorization with permission checks
when: An app has logged in users with different powers (admin, editor, viewer) and every route must check what each role may do, in one place, denying by default.
prompt:
Goal: A permission table and can(user, perm, record) enforced on every route, deny by default.
Steps:
1. permissions.mjs: a frozen ROLE_PERMS = { viewer: ["task:read"], editor: ["task:read", "task:write"], admin: ["*"] } using noun:verb strings.
2. Routes declare needs: router.add("DELETE", "/tasks/:id", { perm: "task:delete" }, handler); startup fails for a route with neither perm nor public: true.
3. Guard before the handler: no user gives 401, a user lacking the perm gives 403 with code forbidden.
4. Ownership next to the table: can(user, "task:write", task) also needs task.ownerId === user.id unless the role holds task:write:any.
5. Load the role from the server session or database each request, never from a client field.
6. Log denials at warn with user id, perm and route.
Quality bar:
- Hidden buttons are cosmetic; the server is the real check.
- A role change applies on the next request.
- A test walks every route and asserts its perm or public flag.
Pitfalls:
- if (user.role === "admin") sprinkled across handlers.
- Profile updates that accept role from the body (mass assignment).
- Failing open when a perm is missing.
Verify:
- [ ] Every route has perm or public.
- [ ] 401 and 403 are used correctly.
- [ ] Single item writes check ownership.
- [ ] Tests prove a viewer cannot reach admin routes.
Output: permissions.mjs, the route guard in server.mjs, test/permissions.test.mjs.

examples.input: admin, editor e leitor com permissoes diferentes na API
examples.output: ROLE_PERMS table, perm per route, startup check, ownership rule, 401 vs 403 tests
